title: Q2 Roadmap & Launch Readiness - Eng + Product Sync
summary: Internal planning sync to align on Q2 product priorities, finalize launch readiness checklist for the upcoming release, review January cache regression incident and agree actions on telemetry and canary criteria.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Start: 09:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan, Samira, Ethan, Priya, Marcus, Carla, Oliver

Summary: quick sync on Q2 roadmap items, finalize launch readiness, follow up on incident review and telemetry gaps.

Topics: Q2 priorities; launch readiness checklist; incident review - KV cache regression; SLA telemetry; rollout/canary plan.

Action items (captured briefly in transcript): owner lines later in doc.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: alright everyone thanks for joining on time, uh let's kick off. we've got about an hour, main goals finalize the launch readiness checklist, quick incident review from jan cache regression, and sign off on the canary criteria.
[00:18] Samira: yep, sounds good. i put an updated timeline in the doc, link in chat, pls take a look after.
[00:28] Priya: quick note, marketing asked for a final feature list by friday so we need to lock down what ships in q2.
[00:36] Marcus: QA is still finishing the stress tests for dedicated pool autoscale, we saw some flaps at high rps.
[00:45] Ethan: that was the same thing related to the kv cache invalidation, i think, there was a prefix evict that caused there was a, um, a mem pressure and fallback to cpu paths, so latency spiked.
[01:05] Samira: right, incident summary on 2026-01-28 a change to prefix caching logic caused larger than expected cache churn when sequence lengths spiked. that triggered fallbacks and some tails hit the slower kernel path.
[01:25] Jordan: is that the one where the KV cache was mis-sized for bursty workloads? sometimes the notes say "K V cache" or "kv cache" in the doc, transcription mismatch.
[01:34] Ethan: yeah apologies for the naming confusion in the notes, but the core issue was eviction policy + our default retention threshold was too low for longer-context requests.
[01:45] Carla: we observed a UX regression too \u2014 streaming responses slowed, partial tokens arrived later which looked like a stall to end users.
[02:00] Priya: important to call out for launch readiness \u2014 we must guarantee baseline tail latency for streaming customers. marketing will need that SLA number.
[02:12] Samira: proposed fixes: bump retention threshold, add smarter prefix aggregation, and add an autoscaler tweak to pre-warm the pool for anticipated bursts.
[02:30] Oliver: on pre-warm, we should be careful about cost impacts. pre-warm during weekday mornings is fine but continuous pre-warm will spike committed capacity.
[02:45] Marcus: QA note \u2014 once the retention bump is in, we need a full regression test in staging with long sequence synthetic traffic and a few spike patterns. estimate two days.
[03:00] Jordan: ok let's walk through launch checklist, i'm reading from the doc: "sec/compliance docs up to date, SOC2 evidence, SSO test, KMS integration check, audit logs, per-route rate limits". who owns SOC2 evidence update?
[03:18] Priya: I'll coordinate with security, but Samira we'll need engineers to confirm the new KMS rotation flow in prod.
[03:26] Samira: noted, i'll pair with Oliver on the KMS smoke test.
[03:33] Ethan: on audit logs \u2014 we currently have token-level tracing in staging but retention policy needs to be validated for the enterprise tier.
[03:45] Jordan: add that to action items. also we need a final runbook for fallback behaviour across model variants \u2014 when dedicated goes down we want predictable fallback to hosted or reduced-model option.
[03:58] Samira: yep we have a draft. question \u2014 do we want automatic fallback or manual opt-in per customer? that affects how we communicate the SLA.
[04:10] Priya: marketing prefers automatic with explicit note that fallback may change latency and cost; product prefers opt-in for security-conscious customers. middle ground: automatic fallback with a customer-configurable policy.
[04:30] Marcus: QA will need to validate fallback path for consistency of outputs, because model variants can produce different scoring on rerank tasks.
[04:44] Carla: UX: show a banner when fallback occurs so support teams can triage faster.
[04:50] Jordan: good \u2014 add banner to support runbook.
[04:58] Ethan: circling back to telemetry \u2014 we lack one signal: end-to-end token latency percentiles per-customer across model variants. we have per-token server metrics but not stitched client-perceived latencies.
[05:18] Samira: can we add a synthetic client monitor to measure that? maybe a small runner that sends representative prompts and records full roundtrip RTT.
[05:30] Oliver: yes, we have infra for synthetic monitors but need to parameterize by sequence length and concurrency. i'll take that on.
[05:40] Priya: who will own the canary criteria? i want to be clear so we can sign off: success = 99th percentile latency under X ms, error rate < Y, quality regression < Z on eval set.
[05:56] Jordan: product defines thresholds (Priya), engineering defines monitoring and rollback automation (Samira/Ethan). quality regression threshold should be measured with the eval set we discussed last week.
[06:10] Priya: i'll prepare the eval pass and the quality metric definition by thursday.
[06:18] Marcus: QA will run canary tests for three days with production traffic shadowing and then a 24h ramp if we pass.
[06:30] Jordan: timeline check \u2014 we aim to start canary next monday, full rollout later in the quarter. any blockers?
[06:40] Samira: the main blocker is the autoscaler tweak and the KV retention change, both are in progress but not yet merged.
[06:50] Ethan: i have a PR for the retention change, waiting on final perf numbers from microbench. should land by thursday if no regressions.
[07:02] Carla: UX note \u2014 we need to validate streaming UX on mobile under poor network conditions.
[07:12] Marcus: good call, QA will include cell network sims. add to checklist.
[07:20] Jordan: okay going into incident postmortem quick recap \u2014 root cause, actions taken, preventive steps. samira do you want to summarize?
[07:30] Samira: sure. root cause: retention threshold too low + eviction behavior during long-context bursts. immediate fix: rollback the new prefix eviction, we reverted last friday; next steps: retention bump, smarter prefix aggregation, better synthetic spike tests.
[07:50] Jordan: any estimation on frequency? how often do these bursts happen in prod?
[07:58] Ethan: rare but high impact - roughly 1-2% of requests are long-context and if they cluster they expose the problem. we've added telemetry to flag density of long-context clustered by customer.
[08:15] Priya: that's important for enterprise customers that run long prompts or long conversations like doc summarization.
[08:28] Jordan: okay action items we'll capture in the doc. moving on to launch readiness checklist items we still need to close: KMS test, SOC2 evidence update, synthetic telemetry for E2E latency, QA regression for retention change, canary criteria finalization, marketing feature list.
[08:48] Marcus: also need capacity plan sign-off from finance for pre-warm numbers.
[08:56] Oliver: finance is asking for cost delta for pre-warm vs on-demand. i'll produce a per-day estimate.
[09:05] Samira: on canary rollback automation \u2014 if 95th or 99th percentile exceeds threshold for N minutes we auto-rollback. we need to agree N and thresholds.
[09:18] Priya: propose 99th < 350ms for short prompts, < 700ms for long-context; error rate < 0.2% over 10 minutes. quality regression < 2% on eval.
[09:30] Jordan: sounds reasonable as a starting point. we'll iterate.
[09:36] Marcus: QA will document test matrix and acceptance criteria.
[09:42] Carla: also want to prepare support KB with troubleshooting steps for streaming slowdowns.
[09:50] Jordan: good. last bit: launch comms - we need to finalize the required collateral: release notes, known limitations, runbooks, and the post-launch monitoring plan.
[10:04] Priya: i'll own release notes and coord with docs and support.
[10:12] Samira: i'll make sure runbooks are in the internal ops repo and link them in the doc.
[10:18] Jordan: any final blockers?
[10:22] Ethan: none that can't be handled this week if PRs land.
[10:28] Oliver: raising one: we need an exec sign-off for the SLA numbers; i'll schedule a 15-min with ops leader.
[10:36] Jordan: okay. lets recap action items and next steps.
[10:40] (overlap) Priya: i'll send the eval asset and the feature list by friday, Marcus will run the regression, Samira + Ethan implement retention/autoscaler changes. Oliver cost estimate. Jordan will coordinate exec sign-off.
[10:58] Jordan: thanks everyone, i'll update the doc with owners and timelines, we'll meet next wednesday for a short check-in.
[11:08] End of recording.

Note: transcript contains typical automatic speech transcription artifacts: occasional mis-heard acronyms, run-on sentences, filler words, and some speaker overlaps.
